gaps.title: No persistent codebase memory; every agent session starts cold
gaps.whyItMatters: Copilot (copilot-08, copilot-09), Cursor (cursor-02), Replit (replit-10) and Cognition (cognition-13) all ship persistent repo context, and Copilot is likely to take it to GA at Universe. Session-forgotten context drives about 31% of AE-KR1 failures and rising AE-KR2 repeat-mistake tickets. Full re-indexing per session dominates the PE-KR1 gap. Memory is the top loss reason against GTM-KR1 and threatens at-risk renewals under GTM-KR3, and therefore CG-1 and CG-2.
gaps.recommendation: Name a single cross-team owner who knows the indexer and move R-14 into Now, with a design doc within a month. Phase 1 has two parts. First, persist the index across sessions, which also unblocks R-01. Second, add an admin-manageable, policy-scoped, audit-logged memory store fed by PR review comments, corrections and repo ADRs, and ship it to top at-risk accounts before renewals. First step: customer interviews on the conventions engineers repeat to the agent every session.

gaps.title: Agents run only on the developer's machine; no cloud sandbox for background agents
gaps.roadmapItem: R-09 Cloud sandbox for background agents
gaps.whyItMatters: Cursor (cursor-08, cursor-33), Copilot (copilot-05, copilot-14), Kiro (amazon-16), Devin (cognition-10), Jules (google-16) and Codex (codex-02) all run agents asynchronously in isolated cloud sandboxes, so buyers expect this in bake-offs. R-09 is tied to PE-KR4 (red, 1 of 5 design partners) and GTM-KR1. A VPC-deployable cloud sandbox would turn Forgeline's on-prem strength into a differentiator for CG-1.
gaps.recommendation: Approve the requested +1 headcount for R-09 and target all 5 design partners live this quarter. Support customer-VPC deployment with tenant isolation (reusing R-07) and issue/Slack triggers. First step: define a remote runner interface alongside sandbox/localRunner.ts so the agent loop can dispatch tasks to a VPC-hosted sandbox.

gaps.title: Trust wedge eroding: competitors ship agent control planes, FedRAMP and per-team model governance
gaps.roadmapItem: R-11 Policy packs (banned APIs, license rules)
gaps.whyItMatters: Copilot's Agent Control Plane GA (copilot-12), Cursor Router admin controls (cursor-26), Kiro FedRAMP High/IL-5 (amazon-17), Devin FedRAMP High in-process (cognition-16), and Copilot data residency (copilot-27) narrow the policy and audit advantage that won Forgeline security reviews. Usage-based billing (copilot-15) raises buyer demand for per-team agent cost controls. Together these put CG-1, GTM-KR1, GTM-KR3 and PR-KR1 at risk.
gaps.recommendation: Extend R-11 into a unified agent governance layer covering policy packs, memory and agent audit export via R-03, and model allow-lists. Pull R-18 per-team agent cost controls forward once R-10 ships. First step: add agent-action and memory events to the audit schema in telemetry so governance covers the new R-14 and R-09 capabilities from day one.

moves.headline: Copilot will make cross-agent memory a GA platform primitive
moves.reasoning: Memory went from Pro/Pro+ early access to public preview on all paid plans within a month and already feeds the coding agent, code review and CLI. Universe is GitHub's established launch venue and is themed on the agentic era. Agent usage is now material: one in three PRs involves an agent, and consumption is up after the billing change. GA plus enterprise governance is the natural next step.
moves.prediction: At Universe 2026 (Oct 28-29), GitHub likely announces general availability of Copilot agentic memory for Business and Enterprise. Memories would be shared across cloud agent, code review, CLI and third-party agents in Agent HQ, with org-level admin and audit controls through the Agent Control Plane.

moves.headline: Cursor fuses Graphite and Bugbot into an agent-to-merge pipeline
moves.reasoning: Cursor bought Graphite explicitly because review and merging became the bottleneck. Bugbot just got 3x faster on Composer 2.5 with a local /review command. Its CEO says 35% of internal merged PRs come from cloud agents. Mobile diff review and merge shows the surfaces are converging on agent-driven merge.
moves.prediction: Cursor will integrate Graphite stacked-PR review with Bugbot and its cloud agents. The likely result is an end-to-end flow where an agent opens a PR, an automated reviewer and security review run, and the agent addresses comments and merges, all managed from desktop, web and the iOS app.

moves.headline: Cursor scales a field sales machine across EMEA and APJ
moves.reasoning: Cursor added a revenue and field-operations leadership function, an APJ regional leadership role and a London EMEA headquarters targeting about 200 staff by year-end. It also shipped team-level controls over which models are used. That combination of capital, regional headcount and admin governance points at large enterprise bake-offs, which are exactly where Forgeline competes.
moves.prediction: Cursor will expand regional enterprise sales and customer-success teams in London and Singapore. It will also lean on admin governance features (router mode restrictions, model allow and block lists) to win regulated, large-seat deals in Europe and Asia.

moves.headline: Cognition sells Devin to regulated enterprises via SIs and guarantees
moves.reasoning: Cognition has stacked SI partnerships (Infosys, Cognizant, LTM), government offerings with a DOE MOU and FedRAMP High in-process, and new offices in London, Japan and Singapore. The $1B+ raise and a results-backed guarantee fund this push. These are precisely the regulated, legacy-codebase buyers Forgeline's trust wedge targets.
moves.prediction: Cognition will announce more SI-packaged managed services (more of the five planned LTM offerings), FedRAMP High authorization for Devin Cloud, and more financial-services and government wins in Europe, Japan and APAC. The AI Productivity Guarantee will be its lever for displacing incumbents.

moves.headline: Devin becomes a proactive, always-on maintenance agent
moves.reasoning: Two July team acquisitions were explicitly about automations and a proactive agent approach. Devin Desktop already offers shared-context Spaces and local and cloud agent management. Devin can manage child Devins and run security swarms, so the orchestration layer for proactive work already exists.
moves.prediction: Cognition will ship proactive Devin automations: incident triage, system-health tasks and self-initiated fixes. They will be built on the TierZero and Interaction Company teams and surfaced through Devin Desktop's Agent Command Center and shared Spaces context.

moves.headline: Codex pushes to be the default enterprise agent
moves.reasoning: Codex grew from 1.6M to more than 5M weekly users and named large enterprise rollouts. It added SI partners and AWS commit-drawdown distribution. The product team now sits in a unified ChatGPT/Codex/API organization and the standalone app was folded into ChatGPT. Bundling plus SI channels indicates a push to become the enterprise default.
moves.prediction: OpenAI will expand the Codex partner program with more systems integrators and move Codex on AWS/Bedrock from limited preview to broader availability. It will package Codex Security for enterprise app-sec buyers, distributed through the unified ChatGPT desktop and enterprise contracts.

moves.headline: Google pushes Antigravity into enterprise via Gemini Enterprise
moves.reasoning: Antigravity reached 2.4M+ weekly active users. Version 2.5.0 just added Gemini Enterprise sign-in and Workforce Identity Federation, and Google sunset Gemini CLI for individuals while exempting enterprise licences. With Gemini 3.5 Pro in testing and a subagent-capable CLI and SDK, the next step is an enterprise consolidation onto Antigravity.
moves.prediction: Google will position Antigravity 2.x, the Antigravity CLI and Managed Agents as the enterprise agent platform under Gemini Enterprise. Expected additions are admin and workforce-identity controls, Gemini 3.5 Pro integration, and migration of Gemini Code Assist enterprise users.

moves.headline: Kiro absorbs Q Developer and targets regulated AWS shops
moves.reasoning: Q Developer sign-ups closed and Kiro was named its successor. Kiro now holds FedRAMP High and IL-4/5, gets frontier models in GovCloud, and ships a web autonomous agent with per-task cloud sandboxes. Amazon mandated Kiro internally and offers startup credits, signalling a full-funnel consolidation play.
moves.prediction: AWS will migrate Q Developer customers to Kiro ahead of the April 2027 end of support. It will sell Kiro Web's autonomous agent with FedRAMP High and IL-5 into government and regulated accounts, likely bundled with AWS Transform for modernization at re:Invent.

moves.headline: Replit becomes the governed app layer on enterprise data platforms
moves.reasoning: Replit opened enterprise engineering and product roles through 2026 and made Enterprise self-serve with SSO/SCIM and audit logs. It launched permission-aware Databricks and Fabric deployments in preview. Strategic investors (Accenture, Databricks, Okta, Visa) and a $1B run-rate target push it toward enterprise data-app distribution, with Skills providing persistent team conventions.
moves.prediction: Replit will move its Databricks and Microsoft Fabric integrations from preview to GA and add more permission-aware data connectors. It will grow self-serve Enterprise with Skills and Custom Instructions as organization-wide governed conventions, and may explore agent payments with Visa.

signals.title: The Impact of AI on Developer Productivity: Evidence from GitHub Copilot (arXiv 2302.06590)
signals.summary: Paper by Sida Peng, Eirini Kalliamvakou, Peter Cihon and Mert Demirer reporting a controlled experiment in which developers with Copilot completed an HTTP-server task in JavaScript 55.8% faster than the control group.

signals.title: Research: Quantifying GitHub Copilot's impact in the enterprise with Accenture
signals.summary: GitHub and Accenture study reported ~30% suggestion acceptance, 88% of Copilot characters retained, +8.69% pull requests per developer, +15% PR merge rate and +84% successful builds.

signals.title: Zillow non-engineers build production routing features with Replit
signals.summary: VentureBeat reported that non-technical Zillow employees help build software on Replit, and their features are part of the customer routing system that connects over 100,000 home shoppers with agents. Zillow was also the only customer named in Replit's July 2025 Microsoft announcement.

signals.title: OpenAI releases Codex CLI as open-source terminal agent
signals.summary: TechCrunch reported OpenAI debuted Codex CLI, a lightweight open-source coding agent that runs locally in the terminal, alongside o3 and o4-mini. OpenAI also planned $1M in API credits ($25,000 blocks) for eligible open-source projects.

signals.title: SWE-PolyBench multilingual coding-agent benchmark released
signals.summary: AWS published SWE-PolyBench: 2,110 instances from 21 repos across Java, JavaScript, TypeScript and Python, with a 500-issue subset, open evaluation harness and retrieval-level metrics.

signals.title: Lenny's Podcast: The rise of Cursor, with Michael Truell (co-founder and CEO)
signals.summary: The CEO discussed Cursor reaching $300M ARR and explained why it builds its own custom models (e.g. for autocomplete) alongside foundation models.

signals.title: AlphaEvolve: Gemini-powered coding agent for algorithm design
signals.summary: DeepMind announced AlphaEvolve, reporting Borg scheduling algorithms recovering about 0.7% of Google's worldwide compute and a FlashAttention kernel speedup of up to 32.5%. It found a 48-multiplication method for 4x4 complex matrices.

signals.title: OpenAI launches Codex cloud software-engineering agent (codex-1) as research preview
signals.summary: OpenAI announced a cloud-based Codex agent powered by codex-1, a version of o3 tuned for software engineering, running each task in its own sandboxed environment to write features, fix bugs and propose PRs.

signals.title: GitHub Copilot: Meet the new coding agent (Microsoft Build 2025)
signals.summary: GitHub announced an asynchronous Copilot coding agent that is assigned GitHub issues, runs in a GitHub Actions-powered environment and submits work as draft pull requests. It launched for Copilot Enterprise and Pro+, with each model request consuming one premium request starting June 4, 2025.

signals.title: Cursor 1.0: Bugbot, Background Agent access to everyone, and one-click MCP install
signals.summary: Cursor 1.0 launched Bugbot (automatic PR review on GitHub), opened the remote Background Agent to all users, and added a beta Memories feature that stores per-project facts from conversations.

signals.title: Series C and Scale: $900M at $9.9B valuation
signals.summary: Cursor raised $900M at a $9.9B valuation from Thrive, Accel, Andreessen Horowitz and DST, citing ARR above $500M and use by more than half of the Fortune 500.

signals.title: Don't Build Multi-Agents
signals.summary: Cognition engineering essay arguing multi-agent architectures are fragile because subagents lack shared context and make conflicting decisions; recommends designs where every action sees full prior context.

signals.title: Monthly premium request allowances now enforced for paid Copilot plans
signals.summary: GitHub began enforcing monthly premium request allowances on Copilot Pro, Pro+, Business and Enterprise, with extra requests available via a spending limit that defaults to $0. GPT-4.1/GPT-4o chat and agent mode and code completions stayed unlimited on paid plans.

signals.title: Effort-based pricing for Replit Agent
signals.summary: Replit replaced its flat $0.25-per-checkpoint Agent charge with effort-based pricing, where simple changes may cost less and complex tasks bundled into one checkpoint may cost more. It also added per-request controls (a more capable model, extended thinking) to choose how much effort the Agent spends.

signals.title: Gemini CLI released as open source (Apache 2.0)
signals.summary: Google launched Gemini CLI in preview under Apache 2.0, with a free tier of 60 requests/minute and 1,000 requests/day via a personal Google account (Gemini 2.5 Pro, 1M-token context).

signals.title: GitHub Copilot Chat extension open-sourced under MIT license
signals.summary: The VS Code team open-sourced the GitHub Copilot Chat extension under the MIT license (repo microsoft/vscode-copilot-chat), calling it the first milestone toward making VS Code an open source AI editor.

signals.title: Clarifying our pricing
signals.summary: Cursor apologized for poorly communicated changes that moved Pro from 500 requests/month to token-based usage ($20 of frontier-model usage at API rates plus unlimited Auto), and offered refunds for unexpected charges from June 16 to July 4.

signals.title: Replit and Microsoft partner to bring vibe coding to enterprise (Azure)
signals.summary: Replit announced a strategic partnership with Microsoft integrating with Azure Container Apps, Azure Virtual Machines and Neon Serverless Postgres on Azure, with Azure Marketplace purchasing described as coming soon. The release states Replit is SOC 2 Type II compliant and cites over 500,000 business users.

signals.title: Firebase Studio adds Agent modes, MCP preview and Gemini CLI integration
signals.summary: Firebase Studio added Ask, Agent and Agent (Auto-run) modes, MCP support in preview, and Gemini CLI inside its terminal.

signals.title: Google hires Windsurf CEO Varun Mohan, co-founder Douglas Chen and R&D staff into DeepMind
signals.summary: Per a Reuters report, Google hired Windsurf's CEO, co-founder and select R&D staff to work on Gemini coding tools, and paid a reported $2.4B in licensing fees for non-exclusive access to some Windsurf technology without taking a stake. Google said the team 'will advance our work in agentic coding'.

signals.title: Kiro agentic IDE announced in public preview (spec-driven development)
signals.summary: AWS previewed Kiro, a VS Code-based agentic IDE that starts from specs rather than code, with waitlist access and Claude Sonnet 4 / 3.7 models.

signals.title: Cognition's acquisition of Windsurf
signals.summary: Cognition signed a definitive agreement to acquire Windsurf (IP, product, brand, business and people); Windsurf cited $82M ARR and 350+ enterprise customers. Cognition said it would invest heavily in integrating Windsurf's capabilities into its products.

signals.title: GitHub Spark in public preview for Copilot Pro+ subscribers
signals.summary: GitHub Spark, which builds full-stack apps from natural language (powered by Claude Sonnet 4) with hosting, data storage, inference and one-click publishing included, entered public preview for Copilot Pro+. Spark messages consume premium requests.

signals.title: Jules exits public beta, with free and paid tiers
signals.summary: Google's async coding agent Jules left beta, powered by Gemini 2.5 Pro. Beta users produced over 140,000 publicly shared code improvements; AI Pro and Ultra tiers offer 5x and 20x the introductory limits.

signals.title: GitHub CEO Thomas Dohmke to step down; GitHub leadership to report into Microsoft CoreAI
signals.summary: Thomas Dohmke announced he would leave GitHub at the end of 2025 to become a founder again. Microsoft did not name a new CEO; GitHub's leadership team reports to Microsoft's CoreAI engineering organization.

signals.title: Kiro pricing revised to vibe/spec requests, then billing bug acknowledged
signals.summary: The Register reported Kiro's revised plans (Pro $20, Power $200, $0.04 per extra vibe request) drew user complaints; AWS said a bug over-consumed requests, reset limits and waived August charges.

signals.title: GSA OneGov 'Gemini for Government' agreement at $0.47 per agency
signals.summary: GSA announced an agreement giving federal agencies Google's Gemini for Government AI suite at $0.47 per year per agency, valid through 2026. Coding tools are not specifically named in the coverage read.

signals.title: Team behind Xcode assistant Alex joins OpenAI's Codex division
signals.summary: TechCrunch reported OpenAI is hiring the team behind Alex (an Xcode AI tool); founder Daniel Edrisian said the team is joining Codex. This was a team hire, not a purchase of the company, and Alex stops new downloads after Oct 1.

signals.title: Replit raises $250M at $3B valuation; ~$150M annualized revenue
signals.summary: TechCrunch reported a $250M round led by Prysm Capital at a $3B valuation. The article says annualized revenue grew from $2.8M to $150M in less than a year, citing $100M ARR in June per Amjad Masad.

signals.title: Agent 3 launch
signals.summary: Replit's changelog announced Agent 3 with upgrades to autonomy, reliability and speed, including unattended runs of up to 200 minutes and App Testing in a real browser with a self-review fix loop. It also introduced Agents & Automations (beta) that run on schedules or connect to Slack and Telegram.

signals.title: GPT-5-Codex released for Codex
signals.summary: OpenAI released GPT-5-Codex, a GPT-5 version tuned for agentic coding and code review, reported at 74.5% on SWE-bench Verified, rolling out across CLI, IDE extension, web, GitHub and iOS.

signals.title: Gemini 2.5 Deep Think reaches gold-medal level at ICPC World Finals
signals.summary: An advanced Gemini 2.5 Deep Think solved 10 of 12 ICPC World Finals problems, including one no university team solved, placing second-equivalent among university teams.

signals.title: Copilot coding agent is now generally available
signals.summary: The autonomous, asynchronous Copilot coding agent became generally available to all paid Copilot subscribers. Tasks can be assigned from issues, the agents panel on GitHub, or VS Code's 'Delegate to coding agent' button.

signals.title: Replit acquires OpenInt (first acquisition)
signals.summary: Replit announced its first acquisition, OpenInt, an integration platform for coding agents that now underpins Replit Connectors. OpenInt Cloud was set to shut down on December 31, 2025, with customers moved to self-hosted solutions.

signals.title: Jules Tools CLI and Jules API preview
signals.summary: Google Labs released Jules Tools, a command-line interface, and opened the Jules API for connecting Jules to CI/CD or Slack-triggered tasks. Also added a memory feature, file selector and environment-variable management.

signals.title: CodeMender: DeepMind AI agent for automated code security fixes
signals.summary: DeepMind described CodeMender, built on Gemini Deep Think, which upstreamed 72 security fixes to open-source projects in six months. All patches are reviewed by human researchers before submission.

signals.title: Codex becomes generally available at DevDay with Slack integration, SDK and admin tools
signals.summary: At DevDay OpenAI declared Codex generally available and added a Slack integration, a Codex SDK to embed the agent in other tools, and admin controls/analytics for workspace administrators.

signals.title: Gemini CLI extensions launch with partner ecosystem
signals.summary: Gemini CLI extensions launched with partners Dynatrace, Elastic, Figma, Harness, Postman, Shopify, Snyk and Stripe. Google said more than one million developers were building with Gemini CLI three months after launch.

signals.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore generally available
signals.summary: AgentCore went GA with Runtime (8-hour executions, A2A support), Memory, Gateway (MCP), Identity and Observability, in nine AWS Regions.

signals.title: The road to better completions: a new custom Copilot completions model
signals.summary: GitHub described its custom completions model (mid-training on ~10M repositories, SFT and a custom RL algorithm), reporting 20% more accepted-and-retained characters, 12% higher acceptance rate, 3x throughput and 35% lower latency.

signals.title: Jordan Ministry of Education pilots Siraj AI learning assistant built with Replit
signals.summary: The Jordanian Ministry of Education began a pilot of Siraj, an Arabic, textbook-grounded AI learning assistant built with Replit, reaching 100,000+ students and teachers and 600,000+ interactions. After the pilot the Ministry plans a nationwide rollout to 1.6M students and 90,000 teachers.

signals.title: Vibe coding experience in Google AI Studio
signals.summary: Google introduced a redesigned Build experience in AI Studio to go from prompt to working AI app, with an App Gallery, Annotation Mode and bring-your-own-key fallback.

signals.title: GitHub Universe 2025: Introducing Agent HQ and mission control
signals.summary: At Universe 2025 GitHub announced Agent HQ, saying coding agents from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Cognition and xAI would arrive within paid Copilot plans, plus mission control for managing agent tasks across GitHub, VS Code, mobile and CLI. It also announced Plan Mode, AGENTS.md custom agents, GitHub Code Quality preview and an enterprise agent control plane.

signals.title: Introducing SWE-1.5: Our Fast Agent Model
signals.summary: Cognition released SWE-1.5, an in-house software-engineering model available in Windsurf, served by Cerebras at up to 950 tokens per second.

signals.title: Introducing Cursor 2.0 and Composer
signals.summary: Cursor shipped Composer, its first in-house coding model, plus a redesigned agent-centric interface that runs multiple agents in parallel via git worktrees or remote machines.

signals.title: Past, Present, and Future: $2.3B Series D at $29.3B post-money
signals.summary: Cursor raised $2.3B at a $29.3B post-money valuation with Coatue, NVIDIA and Google as new investors, reporting over $1B annualized revenue and 300+ employees; funds go to research.

signals.title: Gemini 3 launch: 76.2% SWE-bench Verified, 54.2% Terminal-Bench 2.0
signals.summary: Google reported Gemini 3 scoring 76.2% on SWE-bench Verified and 54.2% on Terminal-Bench 2.0, and called it its best vibe coding and agentic coding model.

signals.title: Google Antigravity agentic development platform enters public preview
signals.summary: Antigravity launched free for individuals with an Editor View and a Manager Surface for coordinating multiple async agents across editor, terminal and browser, producing reviewable Artifacts. Supports Gemini 3 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.5 and GPT-OSS.

signals.title: Kiro generally available with CLI, property-based testing, checkpoints and team plans
signals.summary: AWS's weekly roundup states Kiro reached GA the prior week, adding property-based testing, checkpointing, Kiro CLI and enterprise team plans; 250,000+ developers had used it since preview.

signals.title: Reuters-reported internal memo names Kiro Amazon's recommended AI development tool
signals.summary: Reuters reported a memo signed by Peter DeSantis and Dave Treadwell (confirmed by Amazon) telling engineers not to adopt new third-party AI coding tools and to use Kiro; existing tools remain supported.

signals.title: AWS Transform custom generally available
signals.summary: Agentic service for repeatable code transformations (runtime upgrades, framework shifts, language translation) with prebuilt and natural-language-defined transformations; initially US East (N. Virginia) only.

signals.title: AWS Transform named customers: Air Canada, Experian, QAD, Teamfront, Thomson Reuters, Verisk
signals.summary: Amazon's re:Invent press release names these customers as using AWS Transform to reduce technical debt and claims up to 5x faster full-stack Windows modernization; no per-customer metrics given.

signals.title: Kiro autonomous agent launched in preview as an AWS frontier agent
signals.summary: Preview for Pro/Pro+/Power: runs up to 10 concurrent tasks in isolated sandboxes, uses sub-agents for research, coding and verification, learns from code review feedback, and opens PRs via GitHub issues.

signals.title: Amazon Nova 2 foundation models announced on Bedrock (coding among target areas)
signals.summary: Nova 2 Lite and Nova 2 Pro (preview) were introduced, with AWS highlighting multimodal, coding and agentic workloads.

signals.title: Jules adds Suggested Tasks, Scheduled Tasks and Render integration
signals.summary: Jules gained proactive features: Suggested Tasks (experimental, Pro/Ultra), recurring Scheduled Tasks, and automatic fixes for failed Render deployments. Google's Stitch team runs a daily pod of Jules agents.

signals.title: AWS Transform Composability lets partners build mainframe modernization agents
signals.summary: ChannelDive reported the platform where service providers containerize agents for multi-agent workflows; early contributors named as Accenture, Capgemini, IBM, Infosys, Deloitte and TCS.

signals.title: Graphite is joining Cursor
signals.summary: Cursor reached a binding agreement to acquire code review platform Graphite, framing review and merging as the new bottleneck; Graphite continues operating independently with planned product integration.

signals.title: Copilot memory early access for Pro and Pro+
signals.summary: Copilot memory, which builds repository-specific memories used by the coding agent and code review, became available in public preview (early access) for Copilot Pro and Pro+ users, with more plans planned later.

signals.title: Replit app inside ChatGPT
signals.summary: IT Brief reported Replit launched an integration letting ChatGPT users create, preview and refine apps within the chat, built by Replit Agent, alongside a revamped free tier with daily credits. Replit docs (https://docs.replit.com/getting-started/quickstarts/build-in-chatgpt) note each conversation can only work on the one app it created; date is the trade-press publication date.

signals.title: Infosys partners with Cognition to expand engineering capacity
signals.summary: Infosys is deploying Devin across its organization and global client base, starting in Financial Services; the post describes three models (internal productivity, hybrid human-AI delivery pods, managed service provider) and reports no quantitative metrics.

signals.title: Agentic memory for GitHub Copilot is in public preview for all paid plans
signals.summary: Copilot memory expanded to public preview on all paid plans, sharing validated repository memories across coding agent, code review and Copilot CLI. Memories expire after 28 days and can be managed by repository owners.

signals.title: Devin Review: AI to Stop Slop
signals.summary: Launched Devin Review, a free early-release AI code review tool for public and private GitHub pull requests that groups/explains diffs, offers inline chat, and flags likely bugs by severity.

signals.title: Enterprise engineering roles opened (Enterprise, Enterprise Platform, Enterprise PM)
signals.summary: Replit's Ashby job board lists still-open enterprise-focused roles first published 2026-01-24 (Software Engineer, Enterprise), 2026-02-04 and 2026-03-24 (Enterprise Platform), and 2026-06-18 (Enterprise Product Manager). Dates are Ashby publishedAt values as of 2026-10-12.

signals.title: Jules Planning Critic for auto-approved plans
signals.summary: Jules added a secondary critic agent that reviews plans run without human approval; Google reports a 9.5% reduction in task failure rates.

signals.title: Devin crosses the pond: Cognition opens its London office
signals.summary: Cognition announced a London office focused on European enterprises and said it is building a London customer engineering team; Goldman Sachs, Santander, Citi, BNY, HG Capital and The Access Group are listed as partners.

signals.title: Cognizant partners with Cognition to scale Devin and Windsurf
signals.summary: Cognizant is deploying Devin and Windsurf across its engineering organization and client base, with Cognition embedding forward-deployed AI engineers for project selection, enablement and ROI measurement; no figures disclosed.

signals.title: replit/replit-gemini-extension: Replit extension for Gemini CLI
signals.summary: Replit's GitHub org hosts an MIT-licensed extension that lets users create apps and automations with Replit from the Gemini CLI via MCP authentication. Date is the repository creation date per the GitHub API; it was last pushed 2026-09-29.

signals.title: Codex desktop app for macOS launches for managing multiple agents
signals.summary: OpenAI introduced a macOS Codex app for supervising multiple agents in parallel threads with worktree isolation and in-app diff review.

signals.title: Codex app launch ships with doubled rate limits on paid plans and trial access for Free/Go
signals.summary: Coverage of the app launch reports it is included with ChatGPT subscriptions, with limited-time access for Free and Go users and doubled rate limits on all paid ChatGPT plans.

signals.title: Apple Xcode 26.3 adds agentic coding with OpenAI Codex and Claude Agent
signals.summary: Apple announced Xcode 26.3 with support for agentic coding, allowing agents such as Codex and Claude Agent to work inside Xcode, with capabilities also exposed via MCP.

signals.title: Claude and Codex are now available in public preview on GitHub
signals.summary: Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI Codex became available as coding agents for Copilot Pro+ and Enterprise on github.com, GitHub Mobile and VS Code, with no extra subscription. Each agent session consumes one premium request during the preview.

signals.title: GitHub adds Codex (and Claude) to Agent HQ in public preview
signals.summary: GitHub made OpenAI Codex and Claude available as coding agents for Copilot Pro+ and Enterprise; issues can be assigned to an agent which opens a draft PR, and agents can be tagged in review comments with @codex.

signals.title: GPT-5.3-Codex released
signals.summary: OpenAI released GPT-5.3-Codex, described in search coverage as its most capable agentic coding model to date at that time (page itself could not be fetched; date from multiple sources).

signals.title: Brian McCarthy joins Cursor as President of Global Revenue and Field Operations
signals.summary: Cursor announced Brian McCarthy, previously President and CRO at Rubrik, as President of Global Revenue and Field Operations leading its global go-to-market organization; the announcement cited use by more than 50,000 engineering teams and nearly 70% of the Fortune 1000 as customers.

signals.title: GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark launches on Cerebras hardware
signals.summary: Cerebras and OpenAI launched GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark as a research preview, a speed-optimized model running at over 1,000 tokens/s, available to ChatGPT Pro users in the Codex app, CLI and VS Code extension.

signals.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows are now in technical preview
signals.summary: GitHub Agentic Workflows let users write Markdown workflows that the gh aw CLI compiles into GitHub Actions running Copilot CLI (or other coding agents), with read-only defaults and 'safe outputs' for writes. It is open source (MIT) and built with GitHub Next and Microsoft Research.

signals.title: Kiro available in AWS GovCloud (US) Regions
signals.summary: Kiro IDE and CLI became available in GovCloud US-East and US-West, with IAM Identity Center authentication and MCP support.

signals.title: OpenAI details Codex App Server architecture powering all Codex surfaces
signals.summary: InfoQ reported OpenAI's write-up of the App Server, a bidirectional JSON-RPC protocol that powers the CLI, VS Code extension, web app, macOS app and JetBrains/Xcode integrations; source is in the open-source Codex repo.

signals.title: Jules auto-fixes CI failures and can commit as the user
signals.summary: Jules now watches failed GitHub Actions checks on its own PRs and attempts fixes, and users can choose commit attribution (Jules, user, or co-authored).

signals.title: Mobile: Agent generates React Native iOS apps with Expo path to TestFlight and App Store
signals.summary: Replit's product-team post says Agent is tuned to generate React Native iOS apps from a prompt, using Expo to guide apps to TestFlight and the App Store. Planned next: shared web and mobile projects, RevenueCat in-app payments and Android publishing.

signals.title: Introducing Cognition for Government
signals.summary: Launched a government offering for U.S. defense and civilian agencies, bundling Windsurf (FedRAMP High) and Devin (available in AWS GovCloud) with embedded engineering support.

signals.title: GitHub Copilot CLI is now generally available
signals.summary: Copilot CLI, the terminal-native coding agent, left public preview and became generally available, adding plan and autonomous modes, multi-model support, MCP/plugins/skills/hooks extensibility and enterprise controls.

signals.title: The third era of AI software development
signals.summary: CEO post arguing development is moving from Tab and synchronous agents to autonomous cloud agents; states 35% of internally merged PRs come from agents in cloud VMs and agent users now outnumber Tab users about 2:1.

signals.title: Claude and Codex now available for Copilot Business and Pro; Agent Control Plane GA
signals.summary: Claude and Codex coding agents expanded to Copilot Business and Pro customers. Governance runs through the Agent Control Plane, now generally available, with centralized enablement, policy management and audit logging.

signals.title: We Built a Video Rendering Engine by Lying to the Browser About What Time It Is
signals.summary: Replit Engineering described a deterministic web-page-to-MP4 renderer built on a roughly 1,200-line injected virtual clock, WebCodecs video decoding and server-side FFmpeg audio mixing, with SSRF checks on requests. The post says Replit plans to open-source its implementation.

signals.title: Kiro student program pilot with 11 universities (March 2026)
signals.summary: Amazon later described the program as beginning as a March 2026 pilot with 11 universities in two countries; exact day not given, month used.

signals.title: Fortune: Codex passes 1.6M weekly users; Cisco, Nvidia, Ramp, Rakuten, Harvey named
signals.summary: Fortune reported Codex had more than 1.6M weekly active users, and that Cisco, Nvidia, Ramp, Rakuten and Harvey rolled it out across developer teams; Codex head Thibault Sottiaux said OpenAI wants it to be the standard enterprise agent.

signals.title: Copilot code review now runs on an agentic architecture (GA)
signals.summary: Copilot code review moved to an agentic tool-calling architecture that pulls wider repository context, generally available for Pro, Pro+, Business and Enterprise. It runs on GitHub Actions.

signals.title: 60 million Copilot code reviews and counting
signals.summary: GitHub reported Copilot code review usage up 10X since April 2025, now over one in five code reviews on GitHub, with 12,000+ organizations running it automatically on every PR. It cites WEX reporting about 30% more code shipped.

signals.title: OpenAI launches Codex Security application-security agent
signals.summary: OpenAI announced Codex Security (evolved from Aardvark) as a research preview that builds a threat model, validates vulnerabilities in a sandbox and proposes fixes; OpenAI cited 792 critical and 10,561 high-severity findings across 1.2M+ beta commits.

signals.title: $400M Series D at $9B valuation, led by Georgian
signals.summary: Replit raised a $400M Series D at a $9B valuation led by Georgian, with strategic investors including Accenture Ventures, Databricks Ventures and Okta Ventures. It reported 50M+ users, users from 85% of the Fortune 500, and a target of $1B run-rate revenue by end of 2026.

signals.title: Agent 4 launch: Design Canvas, Plan mode, parallel tasks
signals.summary: Replit's changelog announced Agent 4 as an 'AI creative partner' for apps, designs and slides, with a Design Canvas for mockups before code, Plan mode, parallel task execution and multiplayer collaboration. It also lets users pull data from BigQuery, Linear, Slack and Notion directly from chat.

signals.title: Devin can now Manage Devins
signals.summary: Devin can split large tasks across managed child Devins running in parallel in isolated VMs, with a coordinating session that assigns work, tracks progress and compiles results.

signals.title: Introducing Composer 2
signals.summary: Composer 2, built with Cursor's first continued-pretraining run plus long-horizon RL, scored 61.3 on CursorBench (vs 44.2 for Composer 1.5) and is priced at $0.50/$2.50 per million input/output tokens; a technical report was released.

signals.title: OpenAI to acquire Astral (uv, Ruff, ty) to bring its team into Codex
signals.summary: OpenAI announced it will acquire Python tooling company Astral; the team joins Codex after closing, subject to regulatory approval, and OpenAI said it will keep supporting the open-source tools. Terms were not disclosed.

signals.title: American Optimist Ep 147: Cognition co-founders on the new era of software abundance
signals.summary: Podcast with Cognition's co-founders covering growth in early 2026, the claim that Cognition engineers no longer write code by hand, government IT modernization, and forward-deployed engineers.

signals.title: Research, plan, and code with Copilot cloud agent (formerly coding agent)
signals.summary: Copilot cloud agent (formerly Copilot coding agent) can now work on a branch without opening a PR, produce implementation plans for approval, and run deep-research sessions on a codebase. Date taken from the changelog URL; the page header showed April 1, 2026.

signals.title: Meet the new Cursor (Cursor 3)
signals.summary: Cursor 3 introduced an agent-first workspace showing local and cloud agents (started from desktop, web, mobile, Slack, GitHub, Linear) in one sidebar, with local/cloud handoff and a plugin marketplace.

signals.title: Rubber Duck: Copilot CLI uses a second model family as a reviewer
signals.summary: GitHub introduced an experimental Copilot CLI feature where a model from a different family (GPT-5.4 for Claude orchestrators) reviews the agent's plans and work; on SWE-Bench Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.6 plus Rubber Duck closed 74.7% of the gap to Opus 4.6 (GitHub-reported).

signals.title: Kiro startup credits program relaunched (up to one year of Pro+)
signals.summary: Announced by Deepak Singh (VP DevEx & Agents): early-stage to Series A startups can get up to a year of Kiro Pro+ free, in tiers of up to 2, 10 or 30 users.

signals.title: Introducing SWE 1.6: Improving Model UX
signals.summary: Released SWE-1.6 in Windsurf, running up to 950 tokens per second and free for three months; length-penalty training reduced overthinking and looping.

signals.title: Launching in Japan with Takumi Masai
signals.summary: Cognition expanded into Japan, its first step into Asia, planning a local team across engineering, go-to-market and partnerships; names DeNA and Mizuho Securities (via ULS Consulting) as customers.

signals.title: Takumi Masai named Japan President and General Manager
signals.summary: Cognition announced Takumi Masai, most recently President of Datadog Japan with prior senior roles at IBM, Pivotal, Microsoft and Workday, as Japan President and General Manager.

signals.title: Copilot data residency (US, EU) and FedRAMP-authorized models
signals.summary: Copilot added US and EU data residency for GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency; underlying model hosts are FedRAMP Moderate authorized, but Copilot itself was stated as not yet FedRAMP authorized. Such requests carry a 10% higher model multiplier and Gemini models were unsupported at launch.

signals.title: New self-serve plans for Devin
signals.summary: Introduced Devin self-serve tiers: Free, Pro ($20/month), Max ($200/month), Teams (usage-based, $80/month minimum) and custom Enterprise.

signals.title: Devin in Windsurf
signals.summary: Windsurf 2.0 lets users plan locally, hand work to the cloud agent Devin in one click, and review Devin's pull requests inside Windsurf.

signals.title: Copilot pauses new individual sign-ups and tightens limits
signals.summary: GitHub paused new sign-ups for Copilot Student, Pro and Pro+, tightened usage limits and removed Opus models from Pro, citing service reliability. Refunds were offered through May 20; sign-ups reopened gradually from June 17, 2026.

signals.title: Cursor partners with SpaceX on model training
signals.summary: Cursor said it was compute-constrained and would use SpaceXAI's Colossus infrastructure to scale training of its Composer models; no financial terms were given in the post.

signals.title: OpenAI launches Codex partner program with Cognizant and CGI
signals.summary: OpenAI launched a formal Codex partner program with systems integrators; Cognizant is embedding Codex in its Software Engineering Group and CGI gets early access. Codex had 3M weekly active developers per the article.

signals.title: Replit named 2026 Google Cloud AI Tooling Partner of the Year
signals.summary: Replit's blog says Google Cloud named it a 2026 partner award winner, and cites 50M+ users, use across 85% of the Fortune 500, and enterprise customers Databricks, Zillow, PayPal and Adobe. It notes availability on Google Cloud Marketplace and links to Cloud Run, GKE and BigQuery.

signals.title: Multi-Agents: What's Actually Working
signals.summary: Follow-up to 'Don't Build Multi-Agents' saying multi-agent systems work when one agent writes code and others contribute (reviewer, stronger-model consult, manager of child agents); parallel-writer swarms still see little adoption.

signals.title: Engineering in the fast lane: Mercedes-Benz partners with Cognition
signals.summary: Mercedes-Benz is deploying Devin, Windsurf and Devin for Terminal in R&D and IT across the US, Europe and Asia; in a four-week pilot Devin analyzed 200,000+ lines of COBOL and cut estimated modernization time from eight months to eight days.

signals.title: GitHub Copilot is moving to usage-based billing
signals.summary: GitHub announced all Copilot plans move to usage-based billing on June 1, 2026, replacing premium requests with token-metered GitHub AI Credits; plan prices stay the same (Pro $10, Pro+ $39, Business $19, Enterprise $39) with included credits equal to the price. Completions and Next Edit suggestions remain free, and code review also consumes Actions minutes.

signals.title: Codex comes to AWS and Amazon Bedrock
signals.summary: As part of an expanded AWS partnership, Codex on AWS launched in limited preview, letting developers use existing AWS credentials and count usage toward AWS cloud commitments.

signals.title: Amazon Q Developer IDE plugins end-of-support announced; Kiro named successor
signals.summary: AWS announced new Q Developer sign-ups close May 15, 2026, Opus 4.6 leaves Q Developer Pro May 29, and IDE plugins and paid subscriptions end support April 30, 2027.

signals.title: Devin heads east: Cognition opens its Singapore APAC headquarters
signals.summary: Cognition opened its APAC headquarters in Singapore, covering Southeast Asia, Australia, India and South Korea, and is building a local team in engineering, go-to-market and partnerships; OCBC is a named customer.

signals.title: Richard Spence leads Cognition APAC from Singapore
signals.summary: Cognition's Singapore announcement names Richard Spence as Vice President and General Manager (also listed as Managing Director) leading the APAC business.

signals.title: Simon Green named Cursor President for Asia Pacific and Japan
signals.summary: Former Palo Alto Networks executive Simon Green was named APJ President to run go-to-market and set up a Singapore regional headquarters, targeting Japan, Australia and New Zealand, South Korea, India, Indonesia and Singapore.

signals.title: Individual plans get flex allotments; new $100/month Max plan
signals.summary: Ahead of June 1 usage-based billing, GitHub gave Pro ($10) and Pro+ ($39) extra flex credits (total $15 and $70) and introduced Max at $100/month with $200 total included usage. Completions and next edit suggestions stay unlimited on paid plans.

signals.title: GitHub Copilot app is now available in technical preview
signals.summary: GitHub launched a desktop Copilot app in technical preview for starting isolated agent sessions from issues, PRs or prompts, with repeatable automations and an 'Agent Merge' feature that addresses review comments, fixes checks and merges.

signals.title: Kiro Web launched in preview with autonomous mode
signals.summary: Browser-based Kiro for paid subscribers: multi-repo sessions, GitHub label/`/kiro` triggers, sub-agent autonomous mode, per-task cloud sandboxes and Identity Center controls.

signals.title: Google I/O 2026 developer keynote: Antigravity 2.0, Antigravity CLI, SDK, Managed Agents
signals.summary: The I/O 2026 developer recap announced Antigravity 2.0 and Antigravity CLI with specialized subagents and terminal sandboxing, an Antigravity SDK, and Managed Agents in the Gemini API (a remote-sandbox agent via one API call).

signals.title: Antigravity plans: $100 Ultra tier added, top Ultra cut from $250 to $200
signals.summary: Per Wikipedia's Antigravity article (secondary source), Antigravity 2.0 launch coincided with a $100/month Ultra plan at 5x Pro limits and a cut of the top Ultra plan from $250 to $200/month.

signals.title: Gemini CLI superseded by closed Antigravity CLI; repo stays Apache 2.0
signals.summary: The Register reported Gemini CLI and Code Assist IDE extensions stop serving individual/Pro/Ultra users on June 18, 2026; enterprise licence holders are exempt. The Gemini CLI repo remains Apache 2.0, while Antigravity CLI is not open source as published, drawing developer criticism.

signals.title: Replit Enterprise now self-serve (SSO, SCIM, pooled credits)
signals.summary: Any organization can buy Replit Enterprise on the website with an annual credit commitment, unlimited seats by default and pooled credits, SSO/SCIM, RBAC and audit logs, paid by card or ACH. Deals above $200K or with custom terms still go to sales.

signals.title: More Devins in More Places (Series D)
signals.summary: Raised over $1B at a $26B valuation led by Lux Capital, General Catalyst and 8VC; run-rate revenue $492M. Stated plans include growing headcount and its model training program; says 89% of code committed by its engineers is committed by Devin.

signals.title: Visa makes undisclosed strategic investment in Replit
signals.summary: TechCrunch reported Visa invested an undisclosed amount, and the companies are exploring letting developers and their agents accept payments in Replit via Visa Intelligent Commerce and the Trusted Agent Protocol; no joint product has been announced. It says 1,000+ Visa employees have used Replit.

signals.title: GitHub Copilot and Developer Productivity: An Observational Dose-Response Analysis (arXiv 2606.00438)
signals.summary: Heilman, Kyllo and Murphy-Hill analyzed 43 weeks of data on 16,223 Microsoft Cloud+AI engineers and estimate 40.5% more PRs in highest-usage weeks than zero-usage weeks, with diminishing returns at high usage.

signals.title: Microsoft Fabric collaboration: build enterprise data apps in Replit and deploy into Fabric
signals.summary: Amjad Masad's post announced a collaboration letting enterprises build AI-powered apps in Replit and deploy them within their Microsoft Fabric tenant, enabled by Rayfin, described as an open-source SDK and CLI for app backends. Replit docs describe the integration as preview with an approved-tester requirement.

signals.title: Introducing Devin Desktop
signals.summary: Devin Desktop is billed as the next generation of Windsurf: an Agent Command Center for local and cloud agents, Spaces for shared context, ACP support for third-party agents, and a full backwards-compatible IDE.

signals.title: Microsoft AI introduces MAI-Code-1-Flash for GitHub Copilot
signals.summary: Microsoft AI says it trained MAI-Code-1-Flash from the ground up without third-party distillation, tuned for the GitHub Copilot harness, rolling out to individual Copilot users in VS Code (model picker and Auto). It self-reports 51.2% vs 35.2% for Claude Haiku 4.5 on SWE-Bench Pro.

signals.title: Copilot SDK is now generally available
signals.summary: The Copilot SDK reached general availability across six languages (adding Rust and Java), with multi-client sessions, OpenTelemetry tracing and flexible auth, open to Copilot subscribers and non-Copilot users via BYOK.

signals.title: OpenAI says Codex passes 5M weekly users and expands to knowledge work
signals.summary: OpenAI reported Codex surpassed 5M weekly active users, with knowledge workers about a fifth of users, positioning Codex beyond coding into research, reports and spreadsheets.

signals.title: AI should earn its keep: Introducing the AI Productivity Guarantee
signals.summary: Enterprise guarantee: if Devin's estimated engineering value falls short of what a customer pays over an annual contract, Cognition issues usage credits up to $10M.

signals.title: GitHub Universe 2026 announced for October 28-29
signals.summary: GitHub announced Universe 2026, themed around the agentic era, for October 28-29, 2026 at Fort Mason Center, San Francisco.

signals.title: OpenAI merges ChatGPT, Codex and API product teams under Greg Brockman
signals.summary: Reported (first by WIRED) that OpenAI unified ChatGPT, Codex and the API under Brockman; former Codex head Thibault Sottiaux now leads core product and platform teams.

signals.title: Introducing FrontierCode
signals.summary: Cognition released FrontierCode, a 150-task benchmark written by open-source maintainers that grades whether code would be merged; best reported Diamond (50 hardest tasks) score was 13.4% for Claude Opus 4.8.

signals.title: Bugbot is over 3x faster, 22% cheaper, and finds 10% more bugs
signals.summary: Bugbot, now powered by Composer 2.5, averages about 90 seconds per review (down from about 5 minutes) and adds a /review command to run Bugbot and Security Review locally before pushing.

signals.title: Databricks U2M connector live; integration in public preview
signals.summary: Replit launched a user-to-machine connector for its Databricks integration so Unity Catalog applies individual user permissions to deployed Replit apps, and opened the integration for public preview sign-up.

signals.title: Agent Skills & Custom Instructions
signals.summary: Custom Instructions are persistent workspace-wide guidelines Replit Agent applies to every project, and Skills are reusable instruction files loaded only when a task matches. Together they give the agent standing knowledge of team conventions such as security rules and design systems.

signals.title: Cursor chooses London as EMEA headquarters, targets about 200 regional staff by end of 2026
signals.summary: Pulse 2.0 reported Cursor will open a London headquarters this summer and grow to about 200 EMEA employees by end of 2026, hiring across engineering, go-to-market, customer success and operations; SVP of EMEA Ismail Elmas is quoted.

signals.title: GitHub Copilot app generally available
signals.summary: The GitHub Copilot desktop app became generally available on macOS, Windows and Linux, adding canvases, cloud automations and bring-your-own-model/tools support since preview. A July 2026 changelog extended it to every Copilot plan including Free, with BYOK usable without a subscription.

signals.title: Replit is now available in Claude
signals.summary: Replit became accessible inside Claude: users can send a design from Claude Design to Replit to continue building, or have Claude delegate development tasks to Replit via an official connector.

signals.title: OpenAI launches Patch the Planet with Trail of Bits using Codex and GPT-5.5-Cyber
signals.summary: OpenAI announced Patch the Planet, a Daybreak initiative where Trail of Bits engineers work with Codex and GPT-5.5-Cyber across 19 open-source projects, with HackerOne and Calif supporting triage. Launch date varies by source (June 22-24).

signals.title: Inaugural Vibecon held in New York
signals.summary: Replit recap of its first Vibecon, a two-day event in an industrial space on New York's Lower East Side with speakers including Spike Jonze, Refik Anadol and Reshma Saujani. The post announces no products; date is the recap publication date.

signals.title: Closing the loop: evaluating and improving Replit Agent at scale
signals.summary: Replit described moving Agent evaluation from a pre-release gate to a continuous loop combining offline benchmarks (ViBench), production A/B tests and trace clustering (Telescope). An agent-driven process proposes and tests fixes that engineers review before release.

signals.title: Kiro achieves FedRAMP High and DoD IL-4/5 in AWS GovCloud (US)
signals.summary: AWS announced Kiro IDE and CLI hold FedRAMP High and DoD CC SRG IL-4 and IL-5 authorizations in GovCloud (US) Regions.

signals.title: Cursor Mobile App for iOS
signals.summary: Public beta on paid plans for launching, monitoring and steering cloud agents from a phone, with push notifications, review of diffs and demos, and merging PRs.

signals.title: Introducing Devin Security Swarm
signals.summary: Security Swarm uses parallel agents to find vulnerabilities, confirm exploitability in sandboxes, and open remediation PRs. Date shown as 07.01.26 on the blog index, which lists it chronologically among July 2026 posts.

signals.title: SWE-1.7: Frontier Intelligence at a Fraction of the Cost
signals.summary: SWE-1.7, trained with RL from a Kimi K2.7 base and served by Cerebras at 1000 TPS, scores 42.3% on FrontierCode 1.1 Main versus 43.0% for GPT-5.5 and 46.5% for Opus 4.8 in Cognition's table; available in Devin web, desktop and CLI.

signals.title: Google Cloud AlphaEvolve generally available; BASF, JetBrains, Kinaxis named
signals.summary: Google Cloud made AlphaEvolve generally available on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform after a December 2025 private preview, naming BASF, JetBrains and Kinaxis as early adopters. No quantitative metrics were given.

signals.title: Codex app merged into the ChatGPT desktop app
signals.summary: An IT vendor note reports that on July 9, 2026 OpenAI merged the standalone Codex desktop app into the ChatGPT desktop app for macOS; no official OpenAI announcement was found.

signals.title: Devin is Now FedRAMP High In-Process
signals.summary: Cognition's full platform, including Devin Cloud, entered FedRAMP High in-process status and was listed on the FedRAMP Marketplace, extending authorization beyond Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf).

signals.title: Kiro first-anniversary post cites customers and growth
signals.summary: Kiro states developer numbers double each quarter and cites Loyola Marymount (500 Lambda functions in half a day vs about two months) and Siemens (service built in 2 weeks); also lists four surfaces: IDE, CLI, Web, Mobile.

signals.title: The Self-Driving Company
signals.summary: Replit reported its engineers roughly tripled code output over about six months while review times, reversions and incidents held steady or improved. It attributes this to internal AI agents that investigate incidents, review code and handle business tasks.

signals.title: Welcoming TierZero to Cognition
signals.summary: The TierZero team joined Cognition; Cognition said it will bring TierZero's work on automations (incident handling, keeping systems healthy) into Devin. The post does not use the word 'acquisition'.

signals.title: Cognition Signs MOU with U.S. Department of Energy to Join The Genesis Mission
signals.summary: Cognition signed an MOU with the U.S. DOE to join the Genesis Mission, offering vulnerability remediation, legacy scientific code modernization and engineering capacity, plus in-kind code security scans and complimentary compute for selected teams.

signals.title: Cursor Router: Auto mode now routes each request to a suited model
signals.summary: Auto mode is powered by Cursor Router with Intelligence, Balance and Cost modes; admins can enable it per team, restrict modes and allow or block underlying models, and it is on by default for Teams plans.

signals.title: Alphabet Q2 2026 remarks: Antigravity above 2.4 million weekly active users
signals.summary: Pichai's Q2 2026 remarks cited over 2.4 million Antigravity weekly active users and a Chrome team on track for 8x faster delivery via model-driven refactoring. Gemini 3.5 Pro was described as in testing.

signals.title: Welcoming The Interaction Company
signals.summary: Cognition welcomed The Interaction Company, maker of Poke, a proactive personal AI agent in text messages; Poke stays available and Cognition plans to combine its proactive approach with Devin.

signals.title: Claude Opus 5 added to Kiro; Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5 reach GovCloud
signals.summary: Opus 5 rolled out gradually in IDE, CLI and Web (1M context, 2.2x credit multiplier); a same-day changelog entry brought Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5 to GovCloud (US).

signals.title: LTM Partners with Cognition To Reduce Cyber Risk in Financial Services
signals.summary: LTM and Cognition launched BlueVerse RightLogic, a results-billed managed service using Devin to cut vulnerability backlogs (target 80% of CVE backlog), the first of five planned joint offerings.

signals.title: Cursor Start: INR 649/month plan for developers in India
signals.summary: Cursor launched an India-specific monthly plan at Rs 649 (tax inclusive) with UPI payment, including Grok and Composer models, always-on cloud agents and Cursor for iOS with remote control.

signals.title: Microsoft FY26 Q4 call: GitHub Copilot at 50 million users
signals.summary: In prepared remarks Satya Nadella said GitHub Copilot has 50 million users, Copilot revenue accelerated over 60% quarter-over-quarter, and one in three GitHub pull requests involves an agent; CFO Amy Hood cited stronger-than-expected Copilot consumption after the June billing change.

signals.title: Introducing Replit Design
signals.summary: Replit launched Replit Design, a creative suite with AI-suggested variations, templates, a Mobbin UI reference library and brand design systems. It lets users choose among models including Claude, GPT-5, Gemini, Kimi and GLM, and launched for all users.

signals.title: Antigravity 2.5.0: enterprise sign-in for Gemini Enterprise accounts
signals.summary: Antigravity desktop v2.5.0 added enterprise sign-in for Gemini Enterprise accounts and Workforce Identity Federation.

radar.summary: The market has moved from in-editor assistants to governed fleets of cloud agents that remember a codebase across sessions and learn from review. GitHub, Cursor, Replit and Cognition all ship this, while their enterprise-trust gaps are closing through FedRAMP authorizations, control planes and SI partnerships. Forgeline should staff and ship persistent agent memory (R-14) and cloud background agents (R-09) this quarter, and make both policy-scoped and audit-logged so they extend its trust wedge instead of conceding parity.

patterns.summary: Every major competitor now runs autonomous agents in cloud sandboxes, triggered from issues, Slack, labels or mobile, that open PRs and fix their own CI failures. Cursor reports 35% of internal merged PRs coming from cloud agents and Copilot says one in three GitHub PRs involves an agent. Local-only agents are now a table-stakes gap.

Persistent, repo-scoped memory is converging into a shared primitive across agent, review and CLI. Examples are Copilot agentic memory, Cursor Memories, Replit Skills and Custom Instructions, Devin Desktop Spaces, Jules memory, AgentCore Memory, and Kiro learning from review feedback.

The enterprise-trust moat is commoditizing. Competitors are adding FedRAMP High and IL-5, data residency, agent control planes with audit logging, workforce identity, and SI partner channels (Infosys, Cognizant, CGI, LTM). Many also back this with regional field teams in London, Japan and Singapore.

Vendors are vertically integrating with in-house, speed- and cost-optimized coding models and routers. Examples are Composer 2/2.5 and Cursor Router, SWE-1.6/1.7, MAI-Code-1-Flash, GPT-5.x-Codex and Codex-Spark, and Nova 2. These lower per-task cost under the shift to usage-based pricing.

reveals.why: The autonomous agent (Dec 2025) was pitched as learning from review feedback, AgentCore Memory went GA (Oct 2025), and Kiro Crew (Aug 2026) shipped persistent memory; productising memory in the main CLI followed.
reveals.announcement: Kiro CLI 2.29 ships learned Memory for local sessions

reveals.why: Autonomous agent preview (Dec 2025), Kiro Web preview (May 2026) said more was coming, and cloud sessions plus config sync (Aug 11) preceded GA by three weeks.
reveals.announcement: Kiro Web and cloud sessions reach general availability

reveals.why: Cognition shipped successive in-house models (SWE-1.5 in Oct 2025, SWE-1.6 in Apr 2026) and its May 2026 Series D post explicitly said it would grow its model training program, foreshadowing a larger next-generation model.
reveals.announcement: Introducing SWE-2, Cognition's in-house frontier-cost coding model

reveals.why: Per-project Memories (June 2025), parallel agents in 2.0 (Oct 2025), the CEO's 'third era' post on autonomous cloud agents (Feb 2026, which the Projects post itself cites), and Cursor 3's unified local/cloud agent workspace (Apr 2026) each laid groundwork for long-running, multi-agent, memory-backed Projects.
reveals.announcement: Introducing Projects: coordinator agent delegating to parallel subagents with persistent shared context

reveals.why: Bugbot (June 2025) and the Graphite acquisition (Dec 2025) showed a push past code writing into review; the Firetiger acqui-hire (Aug 2026), a team building production-monitoring agents, preceded the Rollouts launch by about six weeks, and the launch post was written by Firetiger's co-founder.
reveals.announcement: Bots for the last mile: Rollouts and Security Review

reveals.why: Jules API (Oct 2025) and CI auto-fix (Feb 2026) showed Google productizing hosted background agents, and I/O 2026 announced Managed Agents in the Gemini API; the September preview is the matured runtime.
reveals.announcement: Gemini API 'antigravity-preview-09-2026' managed agent (sandboxed, runs code and manages files)

reveals.why: Google kept enterprise customers on legacy tools at the May transition, then added enterprise sign-in in July; September closed the feature gap with terminal and Git support for Enterprise.
reveals.announcement: Antigravity 2.14.0 brings terminal and Git for Enterprise with a new permissions system

reveals.why: Codex Security launched as a research preview in March and Patch the Planet (June) put Codex plus GPT-5.5-Cyber into open-source patching, pointing toward a cloud-run, always-on security product.
reveals.announcement: Codex Security Cloud: scheduled/on-commit repo scanning with cloud-prepared fixes (DevDay)

reveals.why: A single App Server harness across surfaces, enterprise SI/AWS distribution and the July app merge laid groundwork for persistent, device-portable and team-governed environments.
reveals.announcement: Reusable cloud environments and shared team workspaces for Codex (DevDay)

reveals.why: Enterprise and Enterprise Platform engineering roles opened from January 2026, the March Series D brought in Okta, Databricks and Accenture as strategic investors and cited Fortune 500 usage, and June shipped Databricks per-user permissions and workspace-wide Custom Instructions, all ahead of company-wide admin and compliance controls.
reveals.announcement: Enterprise governance tools: audit logs, Admin API, Workspace Settings, Compliance API
